summary: A confirmed inbox forwarding rule on c.aydin@aegean.edu forwards mail to c.aydin.ogr@proton.me via OWA (F2). The rejected impossible-travel claim (Manisa to Frankfurt in 156 min) is a carrier-geolocation artefact; baseline sign-ins on AS60068 and device dev-unk-7f3a already geolocate to Frankfurt. Risk Gate verdict: escalate, confidence 0.7, due to a partial compromise chain with one abuse signal and no confirmed access.

actions.action: Remove the unauthorized forwarding rule to c.aydin.ogr@proton.me and audit all OWA inbox rules for the account.
Reset the account password, force MFA re-enrollment, and review sign-in history for device dev-unk-7f3a and ASN AS60068.
Search mail logs for messages forwarded to the external Proton address and assess potential data exposure.

contrastive.explanation: Rejecting F2 would leave no surviving signal and the policy would land on benign — the opposite of the human-review path we chose.

risk.rationale: Verified finding F2 (CONFIRMED 0.8) shows an inbox forwarding rule to an external personal Proton Mail address created via OWA, mapped to T1114.003 (email forwarding rule for exfiltration/persistence). This is a confirmed account-takeover indicator independent of the rejected impossible-travel claim, which was explained away as a carrier-geolocation artefact (baseline sign-ins from the same ASN/device already geolocate to Frankfurt). A confirmed external mail-forwarding rule constitutes a confirmed ATO chain, warranting containment. Cited finding: F2.
escalate_reasons: signals of compromise without a confirmed abuse chain
